sn1.35:1.2: For the deities to stand in the air is disrespectful if not downright threatening ([dn3:1.21.1.]()).
sn1.35:6.4: Rarely do the texts mention the Buddha smiling, usually when he arrives at some place of special, hidden significance. (). However, at [thag12.2:11.1]() he is said to have smiled when Sunīta, having gone forth from a low-born family, was honored by the gods. In both cases the Buddha smiled at the point when the gods rightly honored one who had been seen as contemptible.
sn1.35:8.3: Commentary glosses _yadi verāni na sammeyyuṃ_, suggesting a reading _na ce_, weakened for the metre.
